sources.name: Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga — List entry 7789, Gabriel's Gully
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: National heritage list entry reviewed September 2026: Gabriel Read found gold in the gully on 25 May 1861; the Blue Spur and Gabriel's Gully Consolidated Company operated until it was wound up in 1912. Corroborated by the Department of Conservation reserve history (https://www.doc.govt.nz/parks-and-recreation/places-to-go/otago/places/gabriels-gully-historic-reserve/things-to-do/history-of-gabriels-gully/). Representative OpenStreetMap locality point for the gully, not an individual claim. The listing adds that the Gabriel's Gully Sluicing Company took over in 1912 and that mining finally ended in the 1930s; 1912 therefore closes only the documented company phase. Adversarially re-verified 24 September 2026.

sources.name: University of Tasmania Library Special & Rare Collections — Mount Bischoff Tin Mine administrative history
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: Archival authority record reviewed September 2026: Mount Bischoff's tin-bearing cassiterite was discovered by James 'Philosopher' Smith at Tinstone Creek in 1871. Applied to the existing ICMM Mt. Bischoff tin occurrence 0.5 km from the OpenStreetMap Mount Bischoff peak (https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/3008760336); no production period is inferred.

sources.name: Te Ara — Encyclopedia of New Zealand (Ministry for Culture and Heritage) — Hauraki–Coromandel places: Thames; Hauraki–Coromandel region: Gold mining
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: Government encyclopedia reviewed September 2026: Thames came into existence when gold was discovered in 1867 in the lower Kauaeranga valley; the goldfield made a slow start in 1867 and output steadily declined from 1871 (https://teara.govt.nz/en/hauraki-coromandel-region/page-8). No closure year is given, so no exploitation period is asserted. Representative OpenStreetMap point for Thames town, not an individual claim or shaft. Te Ara refuses automated clients (HTTP 403); both passages were re-read on Internet Archive captures (https://web.archive.org/web/2025/https://teara.govt.nz/en/hauraki-coromandel-places/page-2; https://web.archive.org/web/2025/https://teara.govt.nz/en/hauraki-coromandel-region/page-8). Adversarially re-verified 24 September 2026.

sources.name: Te Ara — Encyclopedia of New Zealand (Ministry for Culture and Heritage) — Hauraki–Coromandel region: Gold mining
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: Government encyclopedia reviewed September 2026: the discovery of gold at Coromandel Harbour in 1852 triggered a rush from Auckland that quickly petered out; the goldfield had little success until well-financed quartz-crushing companies arrived in the late 1860s. No start/end years for extraction are given, so only the discovery is recorded. Representative OpenStreetMap point for Coromandel town. Te Ara refuses automated clients (HTTP 403); the passage was re-read on an Internet Archive capture (https://web.archive.org/web/2025/https://teara.govt.nz/en/hauraki-coromandel-region/page-8). Adversarially re-verified 24 September 2026.

sources.name: Te Ara — Encyclopedia of New Zealand (Ministry for Culture and Heritage) — Hauraki–Coromandel region: Gold mining (Waihī)
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: Government encyclopedia reviewed September 2026: gold was discovered at Martha hill, Waihī, in 1878; low grades, labour shortages and the gold price forced closure of the Martha mine in 1952; it reopened in 1987. Applied to the existing Jasansky et al. Waihi record 0.6 km from the OpenStreetMap Waihī town point (https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/58949475). Only the discovery is added; the historic 1878–1952 working life is not converted into a period on another source's record. Te Ara refuses automated clients (HTTP 403); the passage was re-read on an Internet Archive capture (https://web.archive.org/web/2025/https://teara.govt.nz/en/hauraki-coromandel-region/page-8). Adversarially re-verified 24 September 2026.

sources.name: Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga — List entry 7049, Denniston
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: Category 1 historic place reviewed September 2026: the men who began mining activities at Denniston in 1879; coal was carried by packhorse until the incline was completed in 1880, and the incline delivered coal from 1880 to 1967. Applied to the existing GEM Escarpment Coal Mine, which GEM locates in Denniston (https://www.gem.wiki/Escarpment_Coal_Mine), 4.5 km from the OpenStreetMap Denniston point (https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/313829192). This is a coalfield-level attestation of known, worked coal on the Denniston plateau, not a claim that the modern Escarpment pit operated in 1879.

sources.name: Australian Heritage Database — Australian Cornish Mining Sites: Burra (National Heritage List, place 106304)
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: National Heritage List record reviewed September 2026: the discovery of the Burra Burra copper deposit in 1845; the 'Burra' copper mine operated profitably for thirty-two years from 1845 to 1877 and closed in 1877. The DCCEEW listing page could not be retrieved during verification (no response, no archive capture) and is not relied on. Representative OpenStreetMap point for the National Trust Burra Mine Site, not an individual shaft. Adversarially re-verified 24 September 2026.

sources.name: Australian Heritage Database — Australian Cornish Mining Sites: Moonta (National Heritage List, place 106096)
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: National Heritage List record reviewed September 2026: shepherds discovered the copper ore that became the Wallaroo and Moonta mines in 1859 and 1861; the mine was rich from the outset (c1862) and the Moonta copper mine operated for sixty-one years from c1862 to 1923, closing in 1923. Representative OpenStreetMap Moonta Mines locality position. Verification removed the 1861 discovery entry: it was sourced to a DCCEEW page that could not be retrieved (no response, no archive capture), and the heritage record does not state which of the two finds was Moonta's. Adversarially re-verified 24 September 2026.

sources.name: Australian Heritage Database — Australian Cornish Mining Sites: Moonta (National Heritage List, place 106096), historical context
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: National Heritage List record reviewed September 2026: the discoveries of 1859 and 1861 became the Wallaroo and Moonta mines; the Wallaroo Mining Company's first shipment of 50 tons of ore left Wallaroo Bay in July 1860, and Kadina was laid out near the Wallaroo mines in 1860. No closure year for the Wallaroo mines is given, so no period is asserted. Representative OpenStreetMap Wallaroo Mines locality position.

sources.name: Australian Heritage Database — Castlemaine Diggings National Heritage Park (National Heritage List, place 105683)
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: National Heritage List record reviewed September 2026: gold was discovered at Specimen Gully near Mt Alexander in July 1851 and the Mt Alexander rush began in November; by October 1852 about 350,000 ounces were produced in one month; significant mining continued for many decades. No closure year is given, so only the discovery is recorded. Representative OpenStreetMap Castlemaine locality position within the ~50 km goldfield.

sources.name: Australian Heritage Database — Castlemaine Diggings National Heritage Park (place 105683), history section · cited for Ophir goldfield
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: National Heritage List history reviewed September 2026: the Australian goldrushes began in May 1851 when it was announced that gold had been discovered at Ophir, near Orange NSW. The precise discovery date and discoverer are disputed in secondary literature and are not encoded. No extraction period is asserted. Representative OpenStreetMap Ophir locality position.

sources.name: Australian Heritage Database — Castlemaine Diggings National Heritage Park (place 105683), history section · cited for Ballarat goldfield
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: National Heritage List history reviewed September 2026: gold was found in Victoria in July 1851, with the first real rushes in August and September to Buninyong and what would soon be Ballarat. Applied to the existing Geoscience Australia Ballarat gold operation 3.1 km from the OpenStreetMap Ballarat city point (https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/189820294), as a goldfield-level attestation; the modern mine's own opening is not changed.

sources.name: Australian Heritage Database — City of Broken Hill (National Heritage List, place 105861)
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: National Heritage List record reviewed September 2026: silver was first discovered at Broken Hill in 1883 by Charles Rasp; the silver/lead/zinc Line of Lode has had ongoing mining operations since 1883. DCCEEW summary (https://www.dcceew.gov.au/parks-heritage/heritage/places/national/city-broken-hill) states Rasp discovered the silver, lead and zinc ore seam in 1883. Applied to the existing Jasansky et al. Broken Hill record, 1.5 km from the OpenStreetMap city point (https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/5731495). Production periods are not backfilled. The DCCEEW summary did not answer automated requests and was re-read on an Internet Archive capture (https://web.archive.org/web/2025/https://www.dcceew.gov.au/parks-heritage/heritage/places/national/city-broken-hill). Adversarially re-verified 24 September 2026.

sources.name: Queensland State Archives — Gold at Gympie (Stories from the Archives)
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: State archives article reviewed September 2026: James Nash discovered 'colour' near the Mary River in August 1867 and in October 1867 confirmed the extent of the gold to the Minister for Lands, sparking the Gympie gold rush; the gold mines reached their peak between 1900 and 1910 (the No. 2 South Great Eastern mine peaked between 1899 and 1906). No end of goldfield mining is dated, so no exploitation period is asserted. Representative OpenStreetMap Gympie locality position. The same page states that gold was first discovered near Gympie in 1851 by John Carne Bidwill; because no location is given beyond "near Gympie", verification keeps Nash's 1867 find as the dated goldfield discovery and describes it as the payable find, not the first. Adversarially re-verified 24 September 2026.

sources.name: Queensland Government — Mount Morgan remediation project (abandoned mines)
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: State government page reviewed September 2026: Mount Morgan was founded as a gold mining town in 1882 with its mining operations continuing until November 1990; about 250 tonnes of gold and 360,000 tonnes of copper were extracted; decommissioning followed from March 1991. The page names gold and copper as commodities but gives no start year for copper, so copper is not dated (the builder's note that the page does not state copper was corrected). Coordinate from the OpenStreetMap "Mount Morgan Mine (closed)" industrial area, 0.25 km from the page's own position (-23.641111, 150.372101). Adversarially re-verified 24 September 2026.

sources.name: Victorian Heritage Database — Victoria Hill Quartz Gold Mines, Ironbark (place 8329, Heritage Inventory H7724-0026)
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: State heritage inventory record reviewed September 2026: gold was discovered on Victoria Hill in 1854 and by early 1855 claims covered the whole hill; relics span nearly sixty years of mining from 1854 to 1913, the richest years of Bendigo's quartz-mining industry. Coordinate from the OpenStreetMap Victoria Hill Historic Mine Reserve.

sources.name: Heritage Council of Western Australia inHerit — Hannan's North Heritage Mine (place 07255)
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: State heritage place record reviewed September 2026: on 17 June 1893 Paddy Hannan registered his claim; Hannan's find drew attention to the ore body later known as the Golden Mile (Hannan's claim itself was not on that reef); by the end of 1893 over 100 leases had been taken out in the Kalgoorlie-Boulder area. Corroborated by the State Library of Western Australia (https://exhibitions.slwa.wa.gov.au/s/mewa/page/PatrickHannan). Applied as a goldfield-level attestation to the existing Kalgoorlie record; the modern open-pit production periods are unchanged.

sources.name: State Library of Queensland — Charters Towers: 'The World'
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: State library article reviewed September 2026: in December 1871 a 12-year-old Aboriginal boy, Jupiter Mosman, saw gold in a sandy river bed while looking for lost horses; by February 1872 the goldfield known as Charters Towers was registered and the rush began. Applied to the existing ICMM Charters Towers occurrence, 0.7 km from the OpenStreetMap Charters Towers town point (https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/1974780324); only gold is dated because the source does not date copper. The December 1871 find is recorded in prose only; the dated entry remains the February 1872 registration attestation. Adversarially re-verified 24 September 2026.

sources.name: University of Tasmania — Companion to Tasmanian History: Mount Lyell
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: University reference work reviewed September 2026: in 1882 fine gold shed from the Iron Blow ironstone mass was detected in the Linda Valley and worked by sluicing; in 1892 the Adelaide financiers Kelly and Orr, realising that a fortune in copper was being washed down the sluice boxes, bought the mine and formed the Mount Lyell Mining Company; in 1893 a pyrite orebody was exposed and in 1894 the Mount Lyell Bonanza produced over 850 tons of high-grade copper and silver ore; work stopped at the mine in 1993. Applied to the existing Jasansky et al. Mt Lyell copper record, 1.3 km from the OpenStreetMap Iron Blow point (https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/6520692685); the historical phases are recorded as knowledge only, and silver is not added. The UTAS page refuses automated clients (HTTP 403) and was re-read on an Internet Archive capture (https://web.archive.org/web/2025/https://www.utas.edu.au/library/companion_to_tasmanian_history/M/Mt%20Lyell.htm). The 1892 recognition of copper in the sluicings is noted here but not encoded; the dated copper entry remains the 1893 orebody exposure. Adversarially re-verified 24 September 2026.

sources.name: Texas State Historical Association — Handbook of Texas: Spindletop Oilfield
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: Academic state encyclopedia entry reviewed September 2026: the Spindletop oilfield was discovered on a salt dome south of Beaumont in eastern Jefferson County on January 10, 1901 (the Lucas gusher). No closure is dated in the reviewed passage, so no exploitation period is asserted. Representative OpenStreetMap Spindletop place point on the salt dome, not the gusher well itself.

sources.name: Texas State Historical Association — Handbook of Texas: East Texas Oilfield
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: Academic state encyclopedia entry reviewed September 2026: the field spans central Gregg, western Rusk, southern Upshur, southeastern Smith and northeastern Cherokee counties; since its discovery on October 3, 1930 some 30,340 wells have yielded nearly 5.2 billion barrels. Representative point at Kilgore (Gregg County) inside the 140,000-acre field; the discovery well itself was in Rusk County. No exploitation period is asserted without a dated end.

sources.name: Oklahoma Historical Society — Encyclopedia of Oklahoma History and Culture: Glenn Pool Oil Field
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: State historical society encyclopedia entry reviewed September 2026: the Glenn Number One well was drilled in autumn 1905 and completed on November 22 in the Glenn (Bartlesville) sand; flush production of eighteen to twenty million barrels a year followed in 1906–1908 and 43,520,000 barrels in 1907. Representative OpenStreetMap Glenpool municipal position. Only the discovery is recorded; no field closure is dated.

sources.name: Oklahoma Historical Society — Encyclopedia of Oklahoma History and Culture: Nellie Johnstone Number One
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: State historical society encyclopedia entry reviewed September 2026: April 1897 marked the beginning of Oklahoma's petroleum industry when the first commercial oil well was drilled in Indian Territory; the well was shot on April 15, 1897 and capped until 1899, when a railway allowed oil to be shipped. Coordinate is the OpenStreetMap heritage point for the well.

sources.name: California State Parks — Marshall Gold Discovery State Historic Park
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: State park authority page reviewed September 2026: the park memorializes the site in Coloma where James Marshall first found gold in 1848 on the South Fork of the American River, setting off the Gold Rush. Coordinate from the OpenStreetMap park polygon. No extraction period is asserted for this discovery site.

sources.name: North Carolina Historic Sites — Reed Gold Mine: History
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: State historic site history reviewed September 2026: site of the first documented gold find in the United States after a chance event one Sunday in 1799; the nugget was identified in 1802 and the following year John Reed began the mining operation; underground work began in 1831 and four years later a court injunction closed the mine for a decade; after Reed's death in 1845 the mine was auctioned and was bought in 1895 by Lisle and the Kellys, who ended all underground mining in 1912. Verification split the builder's continuous 1803–1912 span into 1803–1835 and 1895–1912 because the closure is documented and no working between 1845 and 1895 is dated. Coordinate from the OpenStreetMap historic site building. Adversarially re-verified 24 September 2026.

sources.name: Drake Well Museum and Park — official site
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: Official museum site reviewed September 2026: in 1859 the Drake Well struck oil and launched the petroleum industry; the site is presented as the birthplace of the modern petroleum industry. Coordinate from the OpenStreetMap Drake Well Museum grounds at the well site. Earlier knowledge of oil seeps is not converted into a discovery date.

sources.name: The Canadian Encyclopedia — Klondike Gold Rush; UNESCO — Tr'ondëk-Klondike
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: National encyclopedia article reviewed September 2026: gold was discovered in mid-August 1896 on Rabbit Creek, a small tributary of the Klondike River soon renamed Bonanza Creek, leading to the 1897–1899 stampede. UNESCO's Tr'ondëk-Klondike record (https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1564/, read via the UNESCO open-data record whc001 id_no 1564) dates the Klondike Gold Rush to 1896–1898. Applied to the existing MinCan Yukon Consolidated Gold (Klondike dredging) record at Dawson, at the mouth of the Klondike River (1926–1966 production), as a goldfield-level attestation; the dredging periods are unchanged. The OpenStreetMap Discovery Claim (https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/8149596384) lies about 17 km south-east of the MinCan Dawson point, so verification downgraded the entry from discovery to attestation; it is the only gold record within 40 km. Adversarially re-verified 24 September 2026.

sources.name: National Park Service — Keweenaw National Historical Park: Timeline of Michigan Copper Mining 1851 to 1900 · cited for Butte copper
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: Federal park timeline reviewed September 2026: the discovery of copper at a silver mine near Butte, Montana in 1881 transformed the town into 'the richest hill on Earth'; by 1887 Montana mines such as the Anaconda exceeded Michigan production. Applied to the existing USGS Butte vein-deposit record (the 1881 find was in a vein silver mine). Only copper is dated.

sources.name: National Park Service — Keweenaw National Historical Park: Timeline of Michigan Copper Mining 1851 to 1900 · cited for Calumet and Hecla copper
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: Federal park timeline reviewed September 2026: in 1858 surveyor Edwin J. Hulbert found an ancient copper cache that led him to the Calumet conglomerate lode; by 1864 he had secured financing for the Calumet Mining Company and the Hecla Mining Company, which merged as Calumet & Hecla in 1871. The exact year the lode itself was located is not stated, so the 1864 company formation is used as an attestation. Applied to the existing USGS Calumet - Hecla deposit record 0.3 km from Calumet (https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/135021).

sources.name: National Park Service — Keweenaw National Historical Park: Timeline of Michigan Copper Mining, Prehistory to 1850
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: Federal park timeline reviewed September 2026: the Cliff Mine near Eagle River opened in 1845 and closed in 1870; in 1852 it installed a 45-ton steam engine (https://www.nps.gov/kewe/learn/historyculture/copper-mining-timeline-page-2.htm). Coordinate from the OpenStreetMap Cliff Mine tailings area, not the shaft.

sources.name: New Georgia Encyclopedia — Gold Rush (David Williams, Valdosta State University)
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: Academic state encyclopedia article reviewed September 2026: popular discovery stories are undocumented, and no documented evidence for gold in Georgia exists until 1 August 1829, when the Georgia Journal reported two gold mines just discovered; by late 1829 thousands of prospectors arrived, and in spring 1830 four thousand miners worked along Yahoola Creek, from present Dahlonega to Auraria; the Dahlonega branch mint opened in 1838. Representative OpenStreetMap Dahlonega municipal position; not a single mine. Verification moved the attestation from 1829 to 1830: the 1829 Georgia Journal notice reported two gold mines in Habersham County, not at Dahlonega, whereas the spring 1830 report places miners along Yahoola Creek at Dahlonega. Adversarially re-verified 24 September 2026.

sources.name: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Historic Centre of Zacatecas (676)
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: World Heritage description and statement of Outstanding Universal Value reviewed September 2026 through the UNESCO open-data record (https://data.unesco.org/api/explore/v2.1/catalog/datasets/whc001/records?where=id_no%3D%22676%22): Zacatecas was founded in 1546 after the discovery of a rich silver lode and was one of the principal centres of silver mining from the early Spanish period until the 20th century. Applied to the existing USGS Zacatecas district record, 3.0 km from the UNESCO coordinate. Only silver is dated.

sources.name: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Historic Town of Guanajuato and Adjacent Mines (482)
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: World Heritage statement reviewed September 2026 through the UNESCO open-data record (https://data.unesco.org/api/explore/v2.1/catalog/datasets/whc001/records?where=id_no%3D%22482%22): in the mid-16th century Spaniards discovered rich outcrops of silver in the hills of Guanaxhuata; by the 18th century Guanajuato was the world's largest silver-extraction centre, and mining continues. Applied to the existing USGS Guanajuato district record, 2.9 km from the UNESCO coordinate. The year 1550 is a mid-century placeholder, not an exact discovery date.

sources.name: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Historic Town of Ouro Preto (124)
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: World Heritage description reviewed September 2026 through the UNESCO open-data record (https://data.unesco.org/api/explore/v2.1/catalog/datasets/whc001/records?where=id_no%3D%22124%22): founded at the end of the 17th century, Ouro Preto was the focal point of the gold rush and Brazil's golden age in the 18th century; the gold mines were exhausted in the 19th century. UNESCO representative town coordinate, not an individual mine. Dates are century-level only. The same UNESCO record also says "founded in the early 18th century" in its brief synthesis; 1700 is kept only as an approximate century-boundary attestation. The UNESCO point lies 0.4 km from the OpenStreetMap Ouro Preto municipality (https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/314853). The existing USGS gold record "Ouro Preto" (usgs-occurrence:944) sits at [-43.5, -20.9], about 57 km south; it is a coarse district label that cannot carry this period, so this correctly located site is kept and no date is attached to the USGS point. Adversarially re-verified 24 September 2026.

sources.name: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Historic Centre of the Town of Diamantina (890)
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: World Heritage description reviewed September 2026 through the UNESCO open-data record (https://data.unesco.org/api/explore/v2.1/catalog/datasets/whc001/records?where=id_no%3D%22890%22): Diamantina recalls the exploits of diamond prospectors in the 18th century; explorers, diamond prospectors and representatives of the Crown forged its culture in the 18th century. No discovery year is given, so the span is century-level. UNESCO representative town coordinate; the alluvial workings lay in the surrounding rivers.

sources.name: De Beers Group — Our history & heritage
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: Operator history reviewed September 2026: following diamond prospecting in the Vaal River area, the De Beers mine was discovered in May 1871 and the Kimberley mine in July 1871; all De Beers mines closed in 1932 and again in 1940. Applied to the existing USGS De Beers pipe record at Kimberley, about 1 km from the OpenStreetMap De Beers Mine quarry (https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/27311067). Closures are not converted into periods because no reopening dates are given.

sources.name: Petra Diamonds — Cullinan Mine; De Beers Group — Our history & heritage
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: Operator page reviewed September 2026: discovered in 1902, the Cullinan Mine has yielded many iconic diamonds; the De Beers history (https://www.debeersgroup.com/about-us/our-history) independently dates the discovery of the Premier mine near Pretoria to 1902. Applied to the existing USGS Premier record, whose coarse coordinate lies about 3 km from the OpenStreetMap Premier Diamond Mine pit (https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/62642222).

sources.name: The Canadian Encyclopedia — Timmins
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: National encyclopedia article reviewed September 2026: prospecting in the region began in 1906; Benjamin Hollinger, Sandy McIntyre and others made the first large gold discoveries in 1909; the town's fortunes followed the Hollinger, McIntyre and Dome mines. Applied to the existing USGS Hollinger-McIntyre deposit record at Timmins.

sources.name: Online Nevada Encyclopedia (Nevada Humanities) — Comstock Lode
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: State humanities encyclopedia article reviewed September 2026: the Comstock Lode was the first major silver discovery in United States history (about 57% silver and 42% gold by value); the initial discovery was in 1859; the richest ore bodies were found in 1873 and the Comstock produced ore until the 1940s at a reduced rate. Applied to the existing USGS Comstock Lode record about 5 km east of Virginia City (https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/150960509). No period is created because the end is only given at decade level. The Online Nevada page currently returns HTTP 500 to automated clients while still serving the full article text, which was re-read. Adversarially re-verified 24 September 2026.

sources.name: MNopedia (Minnesota Historical Society) — Mesabi Iron Range
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: State historical society encyclopedia reviewed September 2026: iron ore on the Mesabi was recognised by Henry Eames and Christian Wieland in 1866; the Merritt family encountered a large hematite ore deposit near present-day Mountain Iron in 1890, began mining soon after and made the first successful shipment of ore in 1892. Only the 1890 find, located near Mountain Iron, is applied to the existing USGS 'Mesabi Range - Minntac Mine' record 2.7 km from the OpenStreetMap Mountain Iron point (https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/136654); the range-wide 1866 recognition is not attached to a single deposit; the modern taconite operation's own dates are unchanged.

sources.name: Tennessee Encyclopedia (Tennessee Historical Society) — Ducktown Basin Museum
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: State historical society encyclopedia reviewed September 2026: copper mining in the Copper Basin dates to the 1840s; the Civil War stopped mining in 1863; over 24 million pounds of copper were mined from 1865 to 1878; the Burra Burra mine operated from 1899 to 1959 and copper mining continued in the Basin until 1987. Applied to the existing ICMM Copperhill Mine record, 1.8 km from the OpenStreetMap Ducktown municipal point (https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/197158), as a basin-level attestation. 1849 is a conservative end-of-decade bound for 'the 1840s'.

sources.name: Australian Heritage Database — Australian Cornish Mining Sites: Burra (place 106304), South Australian mining context
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: National Heritage List record reviewed September 2026: the copper mines at Burra and Kapunda (a much smaller mine) mark the beginning of Australia's base-metal mining industry; experienced Cornish miners were recruited to open new mines, as happened at Kapunda in 1844; the earlier rich copper carbonate ores at Kapunda and Burra were declining by the time of the 1859–1861 Yorke Peninsula discoveries (https://www.environment.gov.au/cgi-bin/ahdb/search.pl?mode=place_detail;place_id=106096). No discovery or closure year is given, so only the 1844 opening is recorded. Coordinate from the OpenStreetMap Kapunda Historic Mine.

sources.name: NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service — Hill End Historic Site: learn more
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: State protected-area authority page reviewed September 2026: the gold rush hit nearby Bathurst in 1851 and Hill End, swept up in the frenzy, was settled in 1852; the historic site preserves the Colonial Gold Mining Company's roasting kilns and battery buildings. No discovery or end year is given for Hill End itself. Representative OpenStreetMap Hill End locality position.

sources.name: Glencore Australia — Mount Isa Mines: Our history
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: Operator history reviewed September 2026: in February 1923 prospector John Campbell Miles came upon one of the richest known zinc-lead seams in the world by the Leichhardt River and pegged the 'Racecourse' lease, leading to the establishment of Mount Isa Mines. Applied to the existing Geoscience Australia Mount Isa operation (zinc, lead), 1.6 km from the OpenStreetMap Mount Isa town point (https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/247812099).

sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright

sources.name: Namdeb Diamond Corporation — Namdeb at a glance (history)
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright

sources.name: U.S. Geological Survey Bulletin 975-A — Geology of the Huancavelica Quicksilver District, Peru (Yates, Kent and Concha, 1951)
sources.license: Factual metadata; original source content retains its own copyright
sources.description: National geological survey bulletin reviewed September 2026: the history of the district is essentially that of the Santa Barbara mine; the cinnabar deposits were known to the Incas long before the Spaniards arrived; an Indian, Nahuincopa, made their presence known to his master Amador Cabrera in either 1564 or 1566; Cabrera worked them until 1570, when the Crown appropriated them, and the Crown owned them until Peruvian independence in 1821. Only the dated disclosure is recorded (the later of the two years, as an attestation because Inca knowledge was earlier and undated); no exploitation period is added in this verification pass. Representative OpenStreetMap Huancavelica town point; the OpenStreetMap Santa Bárbara point (https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/5271727921) lies 2.8 km south. Adversarially re-verified 24 September 2026.

sources.name: Wikipedia (secondary source) — Oil Springs, Ontario, permanent revision 1303445330

sources.name: Historical exploitation evidence — Berezovskoe gold deposit (Beryozovsky, Urals)

periods.description: Goldfield working from the 1861 rush through the hydraulic-elevating companies of the 1880s, consolidated in 1888, until the Consolidated Company was wound up in 1912. knowledge.description: Gabriel Read found gold in the gully on 25 May 1861, the first payable goldfield in Otago.
Gold discovered in 1867 in the lower Kauaeranga valley, founding the Thames goldfield (quartz-reef gold).
Gold discovered at Coromandel Harbour in 1852; the short-lived rush found little alluvial gold.

periods.description: The copper mine operated from 1845 until mining operations ceased in 1877.

knowledge.description: Copper discovered near Burra Burra Creek by two shepherds in 1845.

periods.description: The Moonta copper mine operated from c1862 (circa start) until its closure in 1923.

knowledge.description: First shipment of 50 tons of copper ore by the Wallaroo Mining Company in July 1860 (the source groups its discovery with the 1859/1861 finds). Extraction attestation, not a discovery date.
Gold discovered at Specimen Gully near Mt Alexander in July 1851; the Mt Alexander rush began in November 1851.
Discovery of gold at Ophir announced in May 1851, beginning the Australian gold rushes.

James Nash found payable gold near the Mary River in August 1867, and his October 1867 report sparked the Gympie rush. The archives also note that John Carne Bidwill first found gold near Gympie in 1851; that find is not located precisely and is not encoded.

periods.description: Gold mining from the 1882 founding of the mining town until November 1990. The 1882 start is the town's founding year and intermediate suspensions are not resolved, so the span is approximate.

sites.name: Bendigo — Victoria Hill quartz gold mines

periods.description: Quartz gold mining documented at Victoria Hill from 1854 to 1913. The source describes the span of surviving mining relics; year-by-year continuity is not asserted.

knowledge.description: Gold discovered on Victoria Hill, Bendigo, in 1854.
Oilfield discovered on January 10, 1901, when the Lucas well gushed oil.
Field discovered on October 3, 1930, by the Joiner well in Rusk County.
Discovery well Glenn Number One completed on November 22, 1905.
First commercial oil well in Indian Territory completed on April 15, 1897. Attestation of a proven oil resource; the well stayed capped until 1899, so no production period starts in 1897.
James Marshall found gold at Coloma on the South Fork of the American River in 1848, setting off the California Gold Rush.

periods.description: Placer mining from 1803 (the year after the 1802 identification), mainly in the farming off-season; underground work from 1831 until a court injunction closed the mine in 1835 ("four years later") for a decade.
Kelly-era working: the mine was bought in 1895, a 10-stamp mill was in place by 1896, and the Kelly family ended all underground mining in 1912.

knowledge.description: Gold nugget found on the Reed farm in 1799 (identified as gold in 1802), the first documented gold find in the United States.
The Drake Well struck oil in 1859, the first oil produced by a drilled well in the Oil Creek valley. Attestation of production, not a discovery of the oil resource (surface seeps were known earlier).

periods.description: Copper mine opened in 1845 and closed in 1870.

knowledge.description: In spring 1830 Niles' Register reported four thousand miners working along Yahoola Creek alone, from present Dahlonega to Auraria. Earliest attestation tied to Dahlonega; the 1 August 1829 first documentary evidence for Georgia gold concerned Habersham County mines and is not attached here.

periods.description: Eighteenth-century gold rush and golden age documented by UNESCO. Century-level coverage; the 19th-century exhaustion is not given an exact year.

knowledge.description: Gold-rush town founded at the end of the 17th century; 1700 is a conservative century-level bound, not an exact discovery or founding year.

periods.description: Eighteenth-century diamond prospecting documented by UNESCO. Century-level coverage, not the exact start of diamond working.

knowledge.description: Kapunda copper mine opened with Cornish miners in 1844. Opening attestation, not a discovery date.

Diamond found by railway worker Zacharias Lewala in 1908 near Kolmanskop, starting the Namibian diamond rush.
Silver ore of Chañarcillo discovered by Juan Godoy in 1832 (aged 32; born 1800), registered as La Descubridora; start of the Chilean silver rush.

Mercury (cinnabar) deposits made known to Amador Cabrera by Nahuincopa in 1564 or 1566 (the later year is used); Cabrera worked them until the Crown appropriated them in 1570. Earliest dated attestation; earlier Inca knowledge is undated.
Free oil found by James Miller Williams in September 1858 while digging a water well, the first commercial oil well in North America (secondary source).
Phosphate discovered on Nauru by Albert Fuller Ellis in 1900; exploitation began in 1906 and the first shipment left in 1907 (secondary source).

knowledge.description: The Jáchymov ore district's mineralisation was discovered in 1516 (Porter GeoConsultancy); the town chronology records a first adit at Konradsgrün in 1512, the mining colony in 1516 and the first silver thalers in 1519. Because the two dates differ, 1516 is recorded as an attestation rather than an exact discovery. No end of silver mining is asserted.

sites.name: Tikhvin bauxite deposits — Boksitogorsk mining area

periods.description: The museum credits the Pechelbronn field with 3.3 Mt of oil from 1735 to 1964 (the first pit is separately dated 1745; large-scale operations restarted in 1916). Field-level interval; interruptions are not resolved. Refining continued until 1970 and is not counted as extraction.

knowledge.description: In 1498 the historian Jacob Wimpheling mentioned oil springs at 'Baechel Brunn' (Pechelbronn). Documentary attestation of surface oil, not a discovery of the producing field.
By the mid-seventeenth century Wietze farmers extracted oil-bearing sand from tar pits and sold the oil as lubricant and medicine. Century-level: 1650 represents 'mid-17th century'.
Early in 1858 the Hanoverian government commissioned, on the advice of Hunäus and Hahse, the first Wietze borehole to open up the oil deposit at the Wallmann tar pit (drilled 1858/59).

periods.description: The museum describes the Bóbrka oil mine as opened in 1854 and still operating in 2026. The interval ends at this dated attestation, not a closure; intermediate interruptions and annual output are not resolved.

knowledge.description: Oil mine opened in 1854 by Łukasiewicz, Trzecieski and Klobassa-Zrencki. An opening date, not a discovery date.

Discovery of crude oil at Digboi in 1889 (Oil India heritage history). Digboi Well No-1 was started in September 1889 and completed in November 1890 as a producer (initial 200 gallons per day). Earlier seep observations in Upper Assam are not dated here. Continuous production to a closure date is not asserted.

sites.name: Bahrain (Awali) oil field — Well No. 1, Jebel Dukhan

knowledge.description: Oil discovered on 2 June 1932 at Well Number One, Jebel Al Dukhan — the first oil discovery on the Arab side of the Gulf. First export shipment in 1934. No closure or continuous production span is asserted.
In 1803 Gasimbey Mansurbeyov extracted oil from two hand-built wells in Bibi-Heybat Bay, 18 m and 30 m from the shore. Earlier undated Absheron oil working is not assigned to this field.

An exploratory oil well was drilled (not dug) to 21 m at Bibi-Heybat on V.N. Semyonov's proposal. The cited chronology dates it to 1846; https://web.archive.org/web/20110606060933/http://www.nefte.ru/history/history25.htm dates it to 1848 and reports that it did not yield oil, hence approximate. The Bibi-Heybat oil is already attested from 1803. No continuous production period is asserted.

A 35 m deep hand-dug oil well at Balakhani bears an inscription giving its construction date and builder (Allah Yar Mammad Nuroghlu): 1594 in the cited chronology, 1593 in other accounts. Documentary attestation of oil extraction, not a field discovery date.

sites.name: Grozny oil field — Starye Promysly (first well No. 1/1)

knowledge.description: On 6 October 1893 drilled well No. 1/1 (spudded 28 June 1893) produced the first oil gusher of the Grozny region at the Old Fields. Earlier artisanal extraction from shallow pits is not dated here. No end of production is asserted.

sites.name: Kudako oil field — Novosiltsev's first well (Kievskoye)

knowledge.description: In 1864 A.N. Novosiltsev leased the oil springs of the Kudako valley and drilled a successful well near Anapa (Kievskoye), registered as a heritage monument 'the first oil well in Russia'. The well No. 1 gusher is dated 3 February 1866 in other accounts. No production period is asserted.

periods.description: Mining commenced in the sixteenth century and continued unabated until closure in 1990. 1600 is the conservative century-level lower bound, not an opening year.

knowledge.description: Modern gold mining at Hutti commenced in 1904. Ancient workings are undated and not used; interruptions in twentieth-century operation are not resolved, so no continuous period is drawn.

The Miike coal mine was placed under government operation in Meiji 6 (1873; 1872 in the UNU study) and modernised; Mitsui acquired it in 1889. Legendary fifteenth-century discovery and eighteenth-century domain workings are not dated because no fetched primary source states them. No closure date is asserted.

periods.description: The operator states the mine has been active since 1517 and currently extracts brine by solution mining. The interval ends at the 2026 attestation, not a closure; interruptions are not resolved.

Salt was exploited in Theresa Mine, the oldest working of the Turda salt mine, between 1690 and 1880. Later extraction in other chambers (e.g. Rudolf Mine) is not dated here, so the mine's final closure is not asserted.

Mining began at the end of the fifteenth century (1500 is the conservative century-level bound) and continued until the mine closed in 1908. The post-war resumption, dated only as 'after the Second World War' until 1962, is not given an invented start year.

knowledge.description: On 8 August 1512 Sten Sture the Younger issued a privilege letter for Salberget, the silver mine. The cow-pasture discovery story is described by the mine itself as a legend and is not dated.

periods.description: Radiocarbon modelling places Early Bronze Age mining start at 2085–1890 cal BC and end at 1735–1485 cal BC (68% probability). The interval uses the latest modelled start (1890 BC) and earliest modelled end (1735 BC), astronomical numbering; archaeological, approximate.

Modern copper mining from the 2 March 1768 discovery of the rich vein until 1904, the last year the source records workings (Morfa Du shafts, precipitation ponds); about 3.5 Mt of ore in total. Interruptions are not resolved.

knowledge.description: The rich copper vein (the 'Great Lode') was found on 2 March 1768 by the miner Roland Puw. The same history records earlier copper finds in difficult wet veins, and Bronze Age mining is recorded as a separate archaeological period. This is therefore an attestation, not the discovery of the resource.

sites.name: Kemerovo — Krasnaya Gorka (Volkov's 1721 coal find, Kuznetsk basin)

knowledge.description: The Mining Encyclopedia credits M. Volkov with discovering a hard-coal deposit on the Tom River bank, at the site of modern Kemerovo, in 1721. This is the first recorded coal find of the Kuznetsk basin. A biography (https://ru.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=149619998) places the find in 1718–1719 and its official registration in 1721, so 1721 is kept as a documentary attestation, not an exact discovery year. No production period is asserted for this locality.

Coal at Lisichya Balka was discovered by N. Avramov in the 1780s–90s and supplied the Lugansk iron works built from 1795; 1795 is used as a conservative attestation of the known deposit, not an exact discovery year.
The presence of coal in the Kizel basin was established in 1783 (basin-level).
Coal mining in the Kizel basin since 1797 (basin-level); no closure is asserted.
Worked since 1745 (the source dates discovery only to the early eighteenth century, so no earlier year is invented). No closure is asserted.

The oxidised copper-ore zone was worked from the middle of the second millennium BC (about 1500 BC, astronomical year -1499); archaeological, approximate. Work continued with interruptions, so no continuous period is drawn.
The deposit was rediscovered by the ore prospectors S. Babin and K. Suleev in 1702; industrial working began in 1709. The mine was mothballed in 1941–45 and reopened in 1959.

periods.description: In the fifth–fourth centuries BC (Classical Athens) the mines smelted at least several thousand tonnes of lead and 10 t of silver a year. The bounds are century-level and use astronomical numbering. Roman and Byzantine traces are not joined into this period.

knowledge.description: The oldest traces of exploitation date to the beginning of the third millennium BC; 2700 BC (astronomical -2699) is a conservative approximate bound.
Mining resumed in 1873; in the nineteenth century ancient waste and slag were also reprocessed for lead, silver and zinc.

sites.name: Alsace potash basin (Mines de potasse d'Alsace, Wittelsheim)

knowledge.description: The Alsace potash salt deposits were discovered in 1904 (basin-level).
Mining of the Alsace potash deposits began in 1910. The later closure is not asserted without a fetched source.
The first Ural (and Russian) diamonds were found in 1829 at the Krestovozdvizhensky placer in the Koiva basin. A discovery, not proof of sustained diamond production here.
Shorsu, the first oil field of the Fergana oil-and-gas region, was discovered in 1880. No production period is asserted.
Silver was worked by the Celts in the third–second centuries BC; the end of the second century BC (astronomical -100) is used as a conservative century-level bound.

By 1740 annual output reached 600 kg of gold and 22.7 t of silver. The seventeenth–eighteenth-century peak also saw the first use of gunpowder for driving mine workings (1627). That milestone does not name a commodity, so gold is dated only from the 1740 output. Continuous production between dated observations is not asserted.

sites.name: Miri oil field — Canada Hill (Oil Well No. 1)

knowledge.description: Oil production at the Miri field began in 1910 (the first oil production in Malaysia). No closure or continuous span is asserted.

sites.name: Nerchinsk mining district — Nerchinsky Zavod silver works

knowledge.description: The Nerchinsk silver-smelting works was built in 1704. Silver-lead-zinc deposits in the district were worked from the early eighteenth century, and output peaked at more than 10 t of silver in 1774. This is district-level evidence, so no continuous period is drawn.
Industrial development of the Sadon deposit from 1852 (working since the 1840s, not given an exact year); silver from it was used for St Isaac's Cathedral.
In 1923–25 the Sadon mine was the only Soviet producer of lead-zinc ores (100% of zinc); zinc is not backdated to the nineteenth century.

First documentary information on the Baskunchak salt lake in I.I. Lepyokhin's work (1768), followed by P.S. Pallas (1773). Salt extraction was mechanised in 1931; earlier artisanal production is not given invented dates.
The Xikuangshan antimony deposit has been exploited since 1894. No closure or continuous span is asserted.
Tin (cassiterite) discovered by James 'Philosopher' Smith at Tinstone Creek, Mount Bischoff, in 1871. Discovery only; no production span is asserted here.
Gold discovered at Martha hill, Waihī, in 1878 (the historic Martha mine closed in 1952 and reopened in 1987).

Coal mining began on the Denniston plateau in 1879 (Fisher, later Banbury, mine). First-extraction attestation for the coalfield, not a discovery date and not the opening of the modern Escarpment mine.
First gold rushes to Ballarat in August–September 1851. Goldfield-level attestation of known, worked gold, not the opening of the modern mine.
Line of Lode silver-lead-zinc ore discovered by Charles Rasp in 1883.
Hannan's reward claim registered on 17 June 1893; over 100 Kalgoorlie-Boulder leases by the end of 1893. Attestation of the Golden Mile goldfield, not a discovery date for the specific ore body.
Charters Towers goldfield registered by February 1872, followed by the rush. Attestation, not a discovery date.
Fine gold from the Iron Blow detected in the Linda Valley in 1882, worked by sluicing.
Pyrite copper orebody exposed by sluicing in 1893; high-grade copper ore produced from 1894.

Klondike placer gold discovered in mid-August 1896 on Rabbit (Bonanza) Creek, a tributary of the Klondike River, about 17 km from this Dawson company record. Goldfield-level attestation for the Klondike dredging record, not the discovery point itself.
Copper discovered at a silver mine near Butte in 1881.
Calumet conglomerate lode known and financed for mining by the Calumet and Hecla companies by 1864 (Hulbert's lead dates from 1858). Attestation, not an exact discovery year.
Rich silver lode discovered in 1546, leading to the founding of Zacatecas.
Rich silver outcrops discovered by Spaniards in the mid-16th century (1550 is a century-level placeholder).
De Beers mine (kimberlite pipe) discovered in May 1871.
Premier (Cullinan) kimberlite mine discovered in 1902.
First large Porcupine gold discoveries by Benjamin Hollinger, Sandy McIntyre and others in 1909.
Initial discovery of the Comstock silver-gold lode in 1859, starting the Rush to Washoe.
Large hematite ore deposit found by the Merritt family near present-day Mountain Iron in 1890; first successful ore shipment in 1892.
Copper mining in the Ducktown Copper Basin dates to the 1840s (1849 used as a conservative decade-level bound).
Zinc-lead outcrops discovered by John Campbell Miles in February 1923.
De Kaap Valley alluvial gold rush of 1883, the first South African gold rush. District-level attestation.
Sheba gold mine established and operating from 1885. Opening attestation, not a discovery date.
Witwatersrand Main Reef discovered in Johannesburg around 1886. Goldfield-level attestation; the source gives 'around 1886'.
First nickel ore extracted at Thio in 1875 (another SLN page gives 1873; the later explicit year is used). Extraction attestation, not a discovery date.
Industrial gold mining began at Obuasi in 1897 with the formation of Ashanti Goldfields Corporation (secondary source). Opening attestation, not a discovery date.
Tsumeb mine production documented from 1905 (to 1996) for copper, lead and zinc (secondary source). Production attestation, not a discovery date.
Development work at the Roan Antelope copper mine was under way by 1928 (the source dates the start of work to 1925). Knowledge attestation, not a discovery date.
Radium-uranium ore body discovered at Shinkolobwe by Robert Rich Sharp in mid-April 1915, during a survey of an old copper prospect. The USGS point is about 41 km from the Shinkolobwe quarry.

Silver ore was discovered in the Kongsberg area in the summer of 1623 and mining began later that year; the last silver was smelted in 1958 after 335 years. Discovery date only; production continuity (including the early-19th-century interruption) is not asserted here.

In 1879 Akaki Tsereteli prepared the Chiatura manganese deposit for mining. The regional administration also cites an 1846 report by Abich, but discovery accounts disagree (1846, 1849, 1879), so the earlier dates are deliberately not used.
Manganese mineralisation was first recognised in the Nikopol Basin in 1883. Basin-level discovery; the marker is a representative basin position.
Mining of high-grade ores began at Marhanets, northeast of Nikopol, in 1886 (Encyclopedia of Ukraine; also PorterGeo).

Iron ore deposits were discovered, in the modern record, in the late 1830s (IntechOpen). 1839 is a conservative decade-level bound. The Encyclopedia of Ukraine notes excavation since Scythian times, so this is an attestation, not a discovery year. The earlier working is not dated here.
Commercial iron ore mining began in 1881 under Oleksander (Alexander) Pol's French-capital company, which mined 37,400 tonnes in its first year.

Discovery in 1690 of an exposed copper vein at Besshiyama; Sumitomo started mining the following year (1691). The mines operated until closure in 1973 (650,000 t of copper). No date is given here for the site's gold or silver co-products.

Copper at Ashio is documented by 1610 (JNTO: first discovered at Mt Bizen Tateyama in 1610; Nippon.com: under Tokugawa administration from 1610). Accounts of earlier sixteenth-century working are not used. The mine ceased operation in 1973. No date is given here for lead, silver or zinc.

The commonly accepted start of silver mining at Ikuno (Kanagase vein, Sengoku period). The legendary 807 discovery is not used. The mine closed in 1973. Copper and gold co-products are not dated here.

Porter GeoConsultancy (Kamaishi – Shinyama, Sahinai, Nippo): magnetite-garnet skarns were worked for iron since 1727 under the Tokugawa shogunate. Treated as an approximate early working attestation, not a discovery; the smelting milestone of 1857–1858 is recorded separately.

By 1858 locally mined Kamaishi magnetite was smelted into pig iron at the Hashino iron mining and smelting site (UNESCO Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution). Documentary attestation of the iron ore, not a discovery date. Copper and gold are not dated here.

The main ground-level tunnel of the Khewra rock-salt mine was developed by Dr H. Warth in 1872 (PMDC). The deposit was worked earlier, but those earlier dates are not asserted without a fetched primary source.

Silver mining at Bawdwin occurred since at least the fifteenth century (estimated historical production about 300 t Ag). Century-level evidence: 1500 is the conservative end-of-century bound, not a start date.

The Burma Corporation was established in 1914 to mine the deeper lead-zinc-silver sulphide ore; peak production followed from 1919 to 1940. Earlier slag retreatment (about 1906) is processing of old dumps and is not used as an extraction date.
Silver mining near Freiberg was described as early as 1168 AD and continued until 1968. Earliest documentary attestation, not a discovery date; lead and zinc co-products are not backdated.
Copper-nickel mineralisation was established in the Noril'sk I deposit by N. Urvantsev in 1920. The vaguer 'first indicated around 1860' report is not used as a date.
Detailed exploration and small-scale exploitation commenced in 1935; mining at Noril'sk-I began in 1943 using forced labour. The Talnakh ores were intersected only in 1960 and are not backdated.

Francisco de Mendoza's 1556 royal expedition located and reported on the abandoned Roman workings of Rio Tinto ('rediscovered'). Earliest dated modern documentary attestation; Roman and earlier mining is not dated here.
In 1727 a small operation began producing blister copper by cementation with water from the Roman workings. Later interruptions (1808–1814 war; cessation by 1870) are not bridged here.
Extensive ancient gold mining at Mahd Adh Dhahab has been dated to between 961 and 922 BC (astronomical year -960 used as the earliest bound). Archaeological dating, approximate.
The ancient deposit was 'rediscovered' in 1932 by K.S. Twitchell. A modern rediscovery, not an original discovery.
The Saudi Arabian Mining Syndicate produced about 22 t of gold and 28 t of silver between 1939 and 1954; commercial production later resumed in 1988. Copper and zinc are not dated here.
Copper and gold were produced from the Lepanto orebody as early as the fourteenth century. Century-level evidence: 1400 is the conservative end-of-century bound.
Organised mining at Lepanto from 1865; later Japanese wartime mining and 1948–1996 production are not bridged into a continuous period.
The Old Sibai copper deposit was discovered in 1913 under a gossanous outcrop (since exhausted). Novyi Sibai was discovered in 1932. Gold is not dated here.

Copper mining at Bor commenced in 1903, following discovery of sub-cropping massive high-sulphidation mineralisation 'at the turn of the 20th century' (no exact discovery year is used). Majdanpek's separate history is not dated here.
The Bayan Obo iron resources were discovered in 1927 (the source adds that they were mined very soon after, without a year, so no earlier production is asserted).
The rare-earth resources of Bayan Obo were recognised in 1935; exploitation began in 1957.

The earliest information on the Gruvberget copper mine dates from the 1644 mining licence; about 1,000 t of copper was produced between 1657 and 1684. The later iron mining at Svappavaara is not backdated.

The Ridder polymetallic deposit was discovered in 1784 by F. Ridder; oxide ore was mined from 1789 to 1861, sulphide ore from 1885 until 1916, and large-scale production resumed in 1944. Only lead, the existing record's category, is dated; other co-products are not backdated.
Copper oxide mineralisation discovered at Almalyk in 1926. Open-pit mining at Kal'makyr began only in 1954 and is not backdated.

The Dal'negorsk borosilicate skarn deposit was discovered in 1946 and put into operation in 1959. The district's earlier lead-zinc mining (from 1907) belongs to separate surrounding deposits and is not attached to this boron record.

Stepan Chumpin's find of magnetite iron ore at Gora Blagodat was registered for the state by V.N. Tatishchev on 14 (25) May 1735; Kushva was founded the same year. Mining of the Blagodat deposit is recorded in the source from 1739.
The presence of coal in the Karaganda basin was established in 1833 (basin-level discovery).
Coal has been mined in the Karaganda basin since 1854; systematic development began in 1930. Continuity between those dates is not asserted.

Gold exploitation in the Vitim (Bodaibo) area of the Lena goldfields since 1840; the Lena Gold Mining Partnership was formed in 1853 for the Bodaibo deposit. District-level attestation, not a discovery date.
Rich copper ore discovered on Zmeinaya Gora by the Korostylev prospectors in 1725.
In 1736 F.E. Lelesnov, A.N. Demidov's steward, determined that the Zmeinogorsk ore also contained silver.
From 1744 to 1835 more than 600 t of silver and about 280 t of gold were smelted from ore mined here; underground work ceased in 1840.
The Verkhnekamsk potassium and magnesium salt deposit was discovered in 1925 under the direction of P.I. Preobrazhensky. Older rock-salt working in the basin is not dated here.
Rich iron ores of the Kursk Magnetic Anomaly were first found in 1931 near Korobkovo and Saltykovo (now Gubkin). Production dates are not backdated.
The Tkibuli-Shaori coal deposit has been known since 1847 (deposit-level; attached to a representative mine).
Mining of the Tkibuli-Shaori deposit since 1897 (deposit-level). Continuity is not asserted.
Discovered in 1888 during geological survey work led by A.P. Karpinsky.
Industrial mining of the Degtyarsk copper-pyrite deposit since 1914.

audit.scope: Historically important extraction sites and fields worldwide, 1500–1950, each with its own fetched sources. New sites use the 'historical-world:' prefix. When a deposit already exists in the atlas, only dated discovery or first-production evidence is appended to that site; no duplicate site is created.
audit.coordinates: Representative mine, field or district positions from the cited source or from a gazetteer entry for the named place (OpenStreetMap, GeoNames, national registers). Accuracy is approximate unless the source publishes the point.
audit.verification: Every new site and knowledge update was re-fetched and checked by an independent verifier; unconfirmed items, duplicates and markers farther than about 5 km from the named workings were removed.
